    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    ActivationPolicy
    Controls when and how often a chaos effect fires when its selector matches an operation.
    ActivationPolicy.Builder
    Builder for ActivationPolicy.
    ActivationPolicy.RateLimit
    Fixed-window rate limit on effect applications.
    ActivationPolicy.StartMode
    Controls whether a scenario activates automatically on registration or waits for an explicit ChaosActivationHandle.start() call.
    AgentArgs
    Immutable view of parsed agent arguments.
    AgentArgsParser
    Parses the raw -javaagent: argument string into an AgentArgs value object.
    AgentHookThread
    A thread of the agent that the JDK starts, not the agent: a shutdown hook.
    AgentLog
    The agent's java.util.logging lines.
    AgentSettings
    The agent's settings, resolved once per start: each one is read from the agent argument, then the system property, then the environment variable(s).
    AgentThreads
    Starts and stops the agent's own threads (stressor and expiry threads), so no scenario is ever evaluated for them (L3): each body runs, and each thread is started and stopped, with the dispatch depth raised.
    AsyncChaosEventListener
    A listener the control plane calls on an agent-owned thread, through a bounded queue; created by ChaosEventListener.async(ChaosEventListener).
    BootstrapDispatcher
    Bootstrap-classloader-resident static dispatcher that routes intercepted JDK operations to the chaos runtime.
    BridgeDelegate
    Interface implemented by the agent-classloader side of the bootstrap-to-agent classloader bridge.
    ChannelBuffers
    The buffers of one channel read or write that chaos shapes: limited so the call transfers fewer bytes (a torn write, a trickled read), and marked so one bit of the bytes a read returns can be flipped.
    ChaosActivationConflictException
    Thrown when a scenario cannot be activated because a live scenario with the same id is already active in the same scope.
    ChaosActivationException
    Thrown when a chaos scenario or plan fails to activate due to a runtime conflict or precondition violation that is not a configuration error.
    ChaosActivationHandle
    Live control handle for an activated chaos scenario.
    ChaosActuatorEndpoint
    Spring Boot Actuator endpoint for operating the chaos agent at runtime, with the operations, outcomes and HTTP statuses of the Micronaut and Quarkus endpoints (ChaosManagement).
    ChaosAgentBootstrap
    JVM agent entry point and runtime bootstrap for the chaos testing agent.
    ChaosAgentEnvironmentPostProcessor
    Self-attaches the chaos JVM agent early in the Spring Boot startup sequence, before the application context is refreshed and before most application beans (web server, HTTP clients, connection pools) have been instantiated.
    ChaosAgentEnvironmentPostProcessor
    Self-attaches the chaos JVM agent early in the Spring Boot startup sequence, before the application context is refreshed and before most application beans (web server, HTTP clients, connection pools) have been instantiated.
    ChaosAgentExtension
    JUnit 5 extension that installs the chaos agent once per test JVM and opens a class-scoped ChaosSession for the annotated test class.
    ChaosAgentExtension
    JUnit 5 extension that installs the chaos agent once per test JVM and opens a class-scoped ChaosSession for the annotated test class.
    ChaosAgentExtension
    JUnit 5 extension that integrates the chaos agent into the JUnit lifecycle, providing per-test chaos isolation through ChaosSession scoping.
    ChaosAgentInitializer
    ApplicationContextInitializer that ensures the chaos agent is installed before the Spring application context is refreshed.
    ChaosAgentInitializer
    ApplicationContextInitializer that ensures the chaos agent is installed before the Spring application context is refreshed.
    ChaosArcProducer
    CDI producer that exposes the installed ChaosControlPlane as an application-scoped Quarkus bean.
    ChaosAssertions
    Assertions on chaos activity, for tests that check a scenario actually fired (or never did).
    ChaosAssertions.CountAssert
    Assertions on a count.
    ChaosAssertions.DiagnosticsAssert
    Assertions on diagnostics.
    ChaosAssertions.ScenarioAssert
    Assertions on one scenario.
    ChaosAutoConfiguration
    Auto-configuration that wires the chaos agent runtime into a Spring Boot application.
    ChaosAutoConfiguration.ActuatorConfiguration
    Nested configuration that exposes the Actuator endpoint when both the Actuator classes are on the classpath and macstab.chaos.actuator.enabled=true.
    ChaosContextConfigurer
    ApplicationContextConfigurer that ensures the chaos agent is installed before the Micronaut ApplicationContext starts.
    ChaosControlPlane
    Primary entry point to the chaos agent runtime.
    ChaosDecisionRecorder
    Records which matches of each scenario took effect, so a run can be replayed exactly with ActivationPolicy.Builder.replayMatches(java.util.Collection), even when it was driven by an unseeded probability.
    ChaosDiagnostics
    Read-only runtime view of all registered chaos scenarios and agent health.
    ChaosDiagnostics.ActivationFailure
    A record of a failed scenario activation attempt.
    ChaosDiagnostics.FailureCategory
    Categories of scenario activation failure, used for programmatic error handling.
    ChaosDiagnostics.ScenarioReport
    Per-scenario state and counters at snapshot time.
    ChaosDiagnostics.ScenarioState
    Lifecycle state of a registered chaos scenario.
    ChaosDiagnostics.Snapshot
    Immutable point-in-time snapshot of the full agent state.
    ChaosDiagnosticsMXBean
    MXBean interface for the chaos agent diagnostics, registered with the platform MBean server under the object name com.macstab.chaos.jvm:type=ChaosDiagnostics.
    ChaosDispatcher
    The hot-path dispatch of the chaos runtime: the entry points the instrumentation layer calls through the bootstrap bridge (see BootstrapDispatcher), one class per domain — ThreadDispatch, ExecutorDispatch, MethodDispatch, ClockDispatch, RuntimeDispatch, NetworkDispatch, DnsDispatch, FileDispatch, ProcessDispatch, ClientDispatch — over one shared DispatchEngine.
    ChaosEffect
    Describes the chaos behavior applied when a scenario matches an invocation.
    ChaosEffect.AddressFamily
    The address family a ChaosEffect.DnsAnswerEffect keeps.
    ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect
    Skews the JVM clock as observed through System.currentTimeMillis() and System.nanoTime().
    ChaosEffect.ClockSkewMode
    Mode for ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect.
    ChaosEffect.CodeCachePressureEffect
    Fills the JVM code cache by generating and JIT-compiling a large number of unique synthetic classes.
    ChaosEffect.ConnectionResetEffect
    Closes the socket abortively (SO_LINGER 0): the peer sees a connection reset.
    ChaosEffect.CorruptReadEffect
    Flips exactly one bit in the bytes a successful read returned.
    ChaosEffect.DeadlockEffect
    Creates a deadlock between participantCount threads by acquiring locks in conflicting orders.
    ChaosEffect.DelayEffect
    Delays the matched operation by a random duration in [minDelay, maxDelay].
    ChaosEffect.DirectBufferPressureEffect
    Allocates off-heap direct ByteBuffers to exhaust native direct memory.
    ChaosEffect.DnsAnswerEffect
    Reshapes a DNS answer: replaces it (override, IP literals; applied even when the real lookup failed), keeps one address family, shuffles it and limits its size, in that order.
    ChaosEffect.DnsRewriteEffect
    Resolves host instead of the name the application asked for.
    ChaosEffect.Errno
    The errors an ChaosEffect.ErrnoEffect can raise, with the Java exception each becomes.
    ChaosEffect.Errno.Family
    Which operations an error belongs to.
    ChaosEffect.ErrnoEffect
    Fails the operation the way the operating system reports errno, as the Java exception an application catches for it — the native library's ERRNO effect.
    ChaosEffect.ExceptionalCompletionEffect
    Completes a matched CompletableFuture exceptionally before normal completion runs.
    ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect
    Injects an exception at the entry of a matched method, before the method body executes.
    ChaosEffect.FailureKind
    Failure kind for ChaosEffect.ExceptionalCompletionEffect.
    ChaosEffect.FinalizerBacklogEffect
    Creates objects with slow finalizers to back up the finalizer queue.
    ChaosEffect.GateEffect
    Blocks the matched operation on a manual gate until the gate is opened or maxBlock elapses.
    ChaosEffect.GcPressureEffect
    Sustains a target allocation rate to create GC pressure.
    ChaosEffect.HeapPressureEffect
    Allocates and retains heap memory in chunks, simulating a memory leak or spike.
    ChaosEffect.KeepAliveEffect
    Keeps a named thread alive to simulate a thread that refuses to terminate.
    ChaosEffect.MetaspacePressureEffect
    Generates and loads synthetic classes to fill JVM Metaspace.
    ChaosEffect.MonitorContentionEffect
    Creates high contention on one shared ReentrantLock by spawning threads that repeatedly acquire and hold it, simulating lock convoy conditions.
    ChaosEffect.RedirectEffect
    Connects to another endpoint than the one the application asked for.
    ChaosEffect.ReferenceQueueFloodEffect
    Floods the ReferenceHandler thread's queue by creating a large number of WeakReference objects pointing to immediately-unreachable objects, then triggering GC.
    ChaosEffect.RejectEffect
    Rejects the matched operation the way the real call fails: by throwing the exception that call throws, inferred from the OperationType by the runtime (FailureFactory).
    ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect
    Corrupts the return value of a matched method on exit.
    ChaosEffect.ReturnValueStrategy
    Strategy for ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect.
    ChaosEffect.SafepointStormEffect
    Triggers repeated JVM safepoints by calling System.gc() at the configured rate, causing stop-the-world pauses.
    ChaosEffect.SpuriousWakeupEffect
    Causes Selector.select() to return 0 immediately with no ready keys, simulating a spurious wakeup.
    ChaosEffect.StringInternPressureEffect
    Interns a large number of unique strings, growing the JVM's string table: a long table slows every intern() of the application.
    ChaosEffect.SuppressEffect
    Skips the matched operation.
    ChaosEffect.ThreadLeakEffect
    Spawns threads that are intentionally never terminated.
    ChaosEffect.ThreadLocalLeakEffect
    Plants ThreadLocal entries in threads obtained from the common thread pool, simulating the most common form of ThreadLocal memory leak in production: pool threads retaining large request-scoped objects across requests.
    ChaosEffect.TimeoutEffect
    Waits for the socket's own timeout, then throws SocketTimeoutException; never fires when the timeout is infinite.
    ChaosEffect.TornWriteEffect
    Tears a write: a channel write succeeds short, a socket stream write is cut and reset.
    ChaosEffect.TrickleEffect
    Lets each socket read return at most maxBytes bytes.
    ChaosEffect.VirtualThreadCarrierPinningEffect
    Starts pinnedThreadCount virtual threads, each of which holds its carrier for pinDuration per cycle: on JDK 21–23 by sleeping inside a synchronized block (true pinning, no CPU), on JDK 24 and later, where synchronized no longer pins (JEP 491), by spin-waiting (one CPU per held carrier).
    ChaosEffectAppliedEvent
    JFR event emitted each time a chaos effect is applied to a matched JVM operation.
    ChaosEvent
    Immutable event published to ChaosEventListener subscribers on every chaos lifecycle transition and effect application.
    ChaosEvent.Type
    Discriminates the kind of chaos event delivered to ChaosEventListener.
    ChaosEventListener
    Observer for all chaos lifecycle and effect-application events.
    ChaosFactory
    Micronaut Factory that exposes the installed ChaosControlPlane as a singleton bean.
    ChaosHandleRegistry
    Holds the handles of plans the starter activates for the application (the startup plan), so they stop when the application context closes.
    ChaosInstrumentationException
    Thrown when a scenario cannot be activated because the instrumentation it needs cannot be woven into the running JVM.
    ChaosManagement
    The operations of the chaos management endpoints, independent of any web framework: the Spring actuator's /actuator/chaos, Micronaut's /chaos endpoint and Quarkus' /q/chaos route offer the same four.
    ChaosManagement.ActivationResponse
    The outcome of ChaosManagement.activate(String).
    ChaosManagement.HttpResult
    A response of ChaosManagement.handle(String, String, String).
    ChaosManagement.StopAllResponse
    The outcome of ChaosManagement.stopAll().
    ChaosManagement.StopResponse
    The outcome of ChaosManagement.stop(String).
    ChaosManagementBuildStep
    Registers the /q/chaos routes.
    ChaosManagementEndpoint
    The /chaos management endpoint for Micronaut, matching the Spring Boot actuator's /actuator/chaos: GET /chaos — the diagnostics snapshot; POST /chaos with {"planJson": "<plan>"} — activates a plan; DELETE /chaos/{id} — stops a plan activated here, by handle id or plan name; DELETE /chaos — stops every plan activated here.
    ChaosManagementHandler
    Serves /q/chaos, the Quarkus counterpart of the Spring Boot actuator's /actuator/chaos: GET the diagnostics snapshot, POST a plan as the body to activate it, DELETE /q/chaos/<id> to stop a plan activated here, DELETE /q/chaos to stop them all.
    ChaosManagementRecorder
    Builds the /q/chaos handler at runtime initialisation.
    ChaosMeterBinder
    Publishes chaos activity as Micrometer metrics.
    ChaosMetricsSink
    Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
    a second metrics API beside the events: the same count is chaos.applications of chaos-agent-micrometer's ChaosMeterBinder and of chaos-agent-opentelemetry, which a ChaosEventListener on APPLIED events can also produce for any other backend.
    ChaosMicronautExtension
    JUnit 5 extension that installs the chaos agent once per test JVM and opens a class-scoped ChaosSession for the annotated Micronaut test class.
    ChaosOpenTelemetry
    Publishes chaos activity through the OpenTelemetry API: metrics, and span events that mark the traced requests chaos hit.
    ChaosOpenTelemetry.Registration
    What ChaosOpenTelemetry.metrics(ChaosControlPlane, OpenTelemetry) and ChaosOpenTelemetry.spanEvents(ChaosControlPlane) started; closing it stops them.
    ChaosPlan
    An ordered, named collection of chaos scenarios that activate as a unit.
    ChaosPlan.Metadata
    Identity and human-readable description of a chaos plan.
    ChaosPlan.Observability
    Per-plan toggles for the built-in observability integrations.
    ChaosPlanMapper
    Jackson-based serialisation bridge between JSON and ChaosPlan.
    ChaosPlatform
    The supported entry point of the agent's bootstrap module: framework integrations, test code and applications reach the agent through this class, not through ChaosAgentBootstrap or the other bootstrap types, whose signatures may change in any release.
    ChaosPresets
    Ready-made scenarios for the faults production systems actually meet: a full or failing disk, a refused or slow peer, packet loss, a DNS outage, a clock jump, exhausted descriptors or threads.
    ChaosProperties
    Configuration properties for the runtime chaos starter.
    ChaosProperties.Actuator
    Sub-properties controlling the Actuator /actuator/chaos endpoint.
    ChaosQuarkusBuildStep
    Build-time processor that registers the chaos-agent extension with the Quarkus build graph.
    ChaosQuarkusExtension
    JUnit 5 extension that installs the chaos agent once per test JVM and opens a class-scoped ChaosSession for Quarkus-based tests.
    ChaosQuarkusRecorder
    Quarkus build-time recorder that installs the chaos agent at runtime initialization.
    ChaosRuntime
    Thin facade that composes ChaosControlPlaneImpl and ChaosDispatcher.
    ChaosScenario
    Immutable description of a single chaos injection scenario.
    ChaosScenario
    Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
    Use WithChaos: it takes the full plan JSON model (every selector, effect and policy field), works with every test extension, and is honoured by ChaosQuarkusExtension too.
    ChaosScenario.Builder
    Fluent builder for ChaosScenario.
    ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope
    Defines the visibility scope of a scenario.
    ChaosScenarioLifecycleEvent
    JFR event emitted on every chaos scenario state transition: REGISTERED, STARTED, STOPPED, INACTIVE, RELEASED.
    ChaosScenarios
    Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
    The container of the deprecated ChaosScenario; use WithChaos.
    ChaosSelector
    Defines the targeting predicate for a chaos scenario.
    ChaosSelector.AsyncSelector
    Matches CompletableFuture completion operations.
    ChaosSelector.AwsSdkSelector
    Matches AWS SDK for Java v2 operations, optionally by service and operation.
    ChaosSelector.ClassLoadingSelector
    Matches class and resource loading operations.
    ChaosSelector.DnsSelector
    Matches DNS resolution operations, optionally filtering by the hostname being resolved.
    ChaosSelector.ExecutorSelector
    Matches executor submit and worker-run operations, optionally filtering by executor class and submitted task class.
    ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector
    Matches file operations: reads and writes of streams, RandomAccessFile and FileChannel, fsync, truncation, deletion and moves.
    ChaosSelector.HttpClientSelector
    Matches HTTP client send operations across supported clients, optionally filtering by request URL.
    ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector
    Matches JDBC connection-pool and Connection / Statement operations, optionally filtering by a target-name pattern (pool identifier or SQL snippet).
    ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector
    Matches JVM runtime service calls: clock reads, GC requests, process exit, reflection invocations, direct buffer allocations, and object deserialization.
    ChaosSelector.MessagingSelector
    Matches messages sent and received through Kafka clients, optionally by topic.
    ChaosSelector.MethodSelector
    Matches entry to or exit from any method matching the class and method name patterns.
    ChaosSelector.MonitorSelector
    Matches monitor entry and thread parking operations, optionally filtering by the class of the object whose monitor is being entered.
    ChaosSelector.NettySelector
    Matches Netty channel reads and writes on any transport, optionally by the peer.
    ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector
    Matches socket/network operations, optionally filtering by remote host name or IP string.
    ChaosSelector.NioSelector
    Matches NIO channel and selector operations, optionally filtering by channel class name.
    ChaosSelector.ProcessSelector
    Matches the start of child processes and waits for them, optionally by program.
    ChaosSelector.QueueSelector
    Matches blocking queue operations, optionally filtering by queue implementation class.
    ChaosSelector.RedisSelector
    Matches Redis commands sent through Jedis or Lettuce, optionally by command name.
    ChaosSelector.RpcSelector
    Matches gRPC client calls, optionally by full method name (package.Service/Method).
    ChaosSelector.SchedulingSelector
    Matches scheduled task submission and tick operations.
    ChaosSelector.ShutdownSelector
    Matches JVM shutdown hook registration and executor shutdown operations.
    ChaosSelector.SslSelector
    Matches SSL/TLS handshake operations on both SSLSocket and SSLEngine.
    ChaosSelector.StressSelector
    Activates a standalone stressor effect.
    ChaosSelector.StressTarget
    Identifies which stressor to activate when using ChaosSelector.StressSelector.
    ChaosSelector.ThreadKind
    Classifies the thread type targeted by a ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector.
    ChaosSelector.ThreadLocalSelector
    Matches ThreadLocal get and set operations, optionally filtering by the ThreadLocal subclass name.
    ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector
    Matches thread start operations filtered by thread kind and name.
    ChaosSession
    A named session scope that restricts chaos effects to the threads bound to it.
    ChaosSession.ScopeBinding
    A handle that represents a thread's active binding to a ChaosSession.
    ChaosSessionFilter
    Joins the chaos session a request came from: when the request carries ChaosSession.HEADER and a session with that id is open in this JVM, the request thread is bound to it while the request is handled, so session-scoped scenarios apply to the server side of the call.
    ChaosSessionPropagationAutoConfiguration
    Registers ChaosSessionFilter for the test starters, so requests a test sends with X-Chaos-Session run in that test's chaos session.
    ChaosSessionPropagationConfiguration
    The ChaosSessionFilter bean, in servlet applications.
    ChaosStressorSnapshotEvent
    Periodic JFR event that snapshots the current state of all active chaos scenarios.
    ChaosTest
    Meta-annotation combining SpringBootTest and the ChaosAgentExtension so that a test class opts into chaos instrumentation with a single annotation.
    ChaosTest
    Meta-annotation combining SpringBootTest and the ChaosAgentExtension so that a test class opts into chaos instrumentation with a single annotation.
    ChaosTestAutoConfiguration
    Auto-configuration that exposes the ChaosControlPlane as a Spring bean when the chaos extension classes are on the classpath.
    ChaosTestAutoConfiguration
    Auto-configuration that exposes the ChaosControlPlane as a Spring bean when the chaos extension classes are on the classpath.
    ChaosTestKit
    Static helper providing one-liner access to the chaos agent from test code that does not use the JUnit 5 ChaosAgentExtension.
    ChaosUnsupportedFeatureException
    Thrown when a chaos scenario requires a JVM feature or capability that is not available on the current runtime.
    ChaosValidationException
    Thrown during scenario activation when the scenario's configuration violates an API contract.
    CidrBlock
    A block of IP addresses in CIDR notation: "10.0.0.0/8", "2001:db8::/32", or a single address such as "192.168.1.10" (a /32 or /128 block).
    ClientCallExtractor
    Reads the attributes client-library hooks report (topic, gRPC method, Redis command, AWS service and operation, Netty peer) reflectively, so the agent has no compile-time dependency on any of those libraries.
    ClientDispatch
    Dispatch of client-library calls: HTTP clients, JDBC and the messaging, RPC, cache and cloud clients.
    ClockDispatch
    Clock skew of the JVM clock reads: System call sites, java.time, the system Clock and java.util.Date.
    ConfigLoadException
    Thrown when a chaos plan cannot be loaded from any configured source during agent startup.
    DefaultChaosActivationHandle
    Default implementation of ChaosActivationHandle.
    DirectoryTrust
    The trust check of a directory the agent writes code into (bridgeDir): the directory must be neither world-writable without the sticky bit nor owned by another user than the JVM's (root excepted), no directory above it world-writable without the sticky bit or owned by another user, and no link on the configured path owned by another user.
    DnsDispatch
    Dispatch of DNS lookups: forward resolution, the answer returned, and reverse lookups.
    ExecutorDispatch
    Dispatch of executor, scheduler, fork-join, queue and future operations, and of shutdown hooks.
    FileDispatch
    Dispatch of file operations: reads, writes, opens, closes, maps, transfers, fsync, truncation, deletion and moves.
    HookDemand
    Callback through which the runtime asks the instrumentation layer to weave the hooks for a set of operations before a scenario that needs them starts.
    HttpUrlExtractor
    Reflective URL-extraction helpers for intercepted HTTP client calls.
    Internal
    Marks a type, method, field, or constructor as part of the chaos-agent's internal implementation.
    JdbcTargetExtractor
    Reflective pool-identifier extraction helpers for intercepted JDBC pool calls.
    JdkInstrumentationInstaller
    Static-only installer that wires ByteBuddy instrumentation for all JDK interception points.
    JfrIntegration
    Entry point for the optional JFR integration layer.
    LogText
    Makes text safe to put into one log line: the agent's single sanitizer for paths, ids and error messages before they reach a logger or System.err.
    MethodDispatch
    Dispatch of method entry and exit for the methods a MethodSelector names.
    MicronautChaosTest
    Meta-annotation combining MicronautTest and the ChaosMicronautExtension so that a test class opts into chaos instrumentation with a single annotation.
    NamePattern
    A named string-matching predicate used by selectors to filter JVM operations by class name, method name, thread name, resource name, or any other string-valued attribute.
    NamePattern.MatchMode
    Determines the matching algorithm applied by NamePattern.matches(String).
    NetworkDispatch
    Dispatch of socket, socket channel, datagram, selector and TLS operations, with each call's peer and byte count.
    OnTrustedChaosEnablementCondition
    Matches when TrustedChaosEnablement decides that chaos is enabled and the early self-attach did not fail (TrustedChaosEnablement.ATTACH_FAILED_PROPERTY): after a failed attach no chaos bean is created, so nothing attaches again.
    OperationTags
    The operation names the woven advice passes to BootstrapDispatcher.
    OperationType
    Identifies the JVM operation being intercepted or the lifecycle event being signalled.
    PathPattern
    Matches file paths under a directory, or one file.
    ProcessDispatch
    Dispatch of child process starts and waits.
    QuarkusChaosTest
    Meta-annotation that bundles @QuarkusTest and ChaosQuarkusExtension into a single declaration.
    RuntimeDispatch
    Dispatch of JVM runtime operations: gc and exit requests, reflection, direct buffers, serialization, class loading and definition, resources, native libraries, zip, JNDI and JMX.
    ScheduledCallableWrapper<T>
    Wraps a Callable scheduled on an executor so that chaos tick hooks fire around each invocation.
    ScheduledRunnableWrapper
    Wraps a Runnable scheduled on an executor so that chaos tick hooks fire around each invocation.
    SessionHeaderPolicy
    Decides which hosts receive the X-Chaos-Session header.
    StartupConfigLoader
    Resolves and loads a ChaosPlan during JVM agent startup.
    StartupConfigLoader.LoadedPlan
    Result of successfully loading a chaos plan from a configuration source.
    StartupConfigLoader.PlanFile
    The file a configured plan path reads from, with what identifies its contents for change detection.
    StartupConfigLoader.PlanFileStamp
    What identifies a plan file's contents for change detection, taken without reading the file.
    ThreadDispatch
    Dispatch of thread operations (starts, sleeps, parks, monitor entries, thread-local access) and of the session hand-off between threads.
    TrackingChaosControlPlane
    Test-scoped decorator around a JVM-wide ChaosControlPlane that tracks every handle returned from TrackingChaosControlPlane.activate(ChaosScenario) / TrackingChaosControlPlane.activate(ChaosPlan), and by default every session opened and every event listener added through it, so the JUnit extension can release them all when a test finishes.
    TrustedChaosEnablement
    Decides whether macstab.chaos.enabled=true may switch chaos on, based on which property source the value came from.
    TrustedChaosEnablement.Decision
    Outcome of evaluating the enablement flag against an environment.
    TrustedManagementEnablement
    Switches the /chaos management endpoint on when "macstab.chaos.management.enabled" is true and comes from a launch-time local source: system properties, environment variables, the command line, ApplicationContext.run(Map), the application and application-<env> files, the files of micronaut.config.files and Micronaut Test's @Property values.
    TrustedSources
    The trust rule for the switches that enable fault injection or a management endpoint, for the Quarkus and Micronaut integrations (Spring decides with its own property sources).
    TrustedSources.Sourced
    A setting's raw value and the name of the config source it came from.
    WithChaos
    Activates chaos for a test, declared in the same JSON model as the agent's startup plan: either inline (WithChaos.value()) or from a class-path resource (WithChaos.resource()).
    WithChaos.List
    Container for repeated WithChaos annotations.
    WithChaosSupport
    Activates the WithChaos scenarios declared on a test class or method.
